name: Cost causation for large load developers

letters.org: Americans for a Clean Energy Grid
letters.desc: Supports cost-allocation reforms that distribute transmission upgrade costs across the broader customer base while ensuring existing customers are protected and large loads are able to participate fairly and benefit from grid improvements.
quotes: when managed correctly, interconnecting large loads to the grid is a win-win for all customers; the transmission system that serves everyone benefits from additional investment: new costs can be shared among a larger customer base in ways that will mitigate

Proactively planning transmission can increase transparency on the cost and timing of interconnection and identify cost-effective transmission solutions. In particular, when transmission is proactively planned, the costs for interconnection are provided to interconnection customers upfront, and developers have greater clarity on when they can interconnect, reducing uncertainty and the speculative behavior that increases queue timelines.

Require improved regional forecasting for significant loads (75 MW or more). Ensure cost recovery and cost-allocation mechanisms that protect existing customers while allowing large loads to participate fairly in and benefit from the broader grid. Direct proactively planned multi-value high-capacity transmission as part of the solution

letters.desc: IECA supports applying generator-interconnection cost-causation principles to large loads, requiring developers to pay interconnection and study costs and bear stranded-investment risk.
quotes: we also support having the costs of interconnections of large loads, including the costs of all necessary system impact studies, be borne by the developers and customers of such large loads, which should place the risk of stranded investment on those in the best position to manage such risk, i.e., the developers of such large loads.

letters.desc: The filer contrasts shallow charges (which socialise upgrade costs) with deep charges (which assign costs to the data centre). It presents evidence that shallow charging has transferred billions in costs to ratepayers and argues that deeper cost assignment better reflects the causer-pays principle.
quotes: socialising connection charges ("shallow charges") means that the connecting party (i.e. a data centre) does not pay the full cost of the network upgrades, so these are instead borne by other grid users (e.g. residential users).

customers from Illinois, Maryland, New Jersey, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Virginia and West Virginia, collectively paid over US$ 4.3 billion in 2024 for grid investments that were only necessary to accommodate new data centres.

While shallow connection charges can help attract new data centre projects, they can have a negative impact in the local community's cost of living, which could then fuel counter-productive opposition.
Going in the opposite direction, Norway established in their latest policy update that a deep connection charge would be used for projects with capacity above 1 MW.

letters.org: National Association of Regulatory Utility Commissioners
letters.desc: NARUC flags that transmission upgrade costs and other infrastructure investments tied to large load interconnections may unfairly shift onto retail ratepayers if not properly allocated, reinforcing the need for state commission oversight.
quotes: the costs of large load interconnections, including necessary transmission upgrades and other infrastructure investments, may unfairly burden retail ratepayers if not properly allocated

letters.org: New York State Public Service Commission
letters.desc: Large loads add to statewide generation demand and thereby raise costs for all customers. The NYSPSC sees this as a reason for careful state-level cost allocation review, not a federal mandate.
quotes: these large loads will require significant amounts of generation and their appearance on the electric grid will add to the need for more generation to meet statewide electric demand needs and thereby raise the costs for all customers.
